findings.title: Backup codes can be redeemed concurrently
findings.body: This read-modify-write is not atomic: two login requests can both read the same stored code, both pass the membership check, and both write their own stale copy with that code nulled. Both requests then issue authenticated sessions, so a code advertised as single-use can be used more than once. Make validation and consumption conditional/atomic, for example with a transaction that verifies the stored value has not changed before updating it.

findings.title: Backup-code authentication has no test coverage
findings.body: The added test only checks that backup codes can be downloaded and copied; it never logs in with a code or checks that a redeemed code is rejected on reuse. This leaves the core authentication behavior, including its single-use guarantee, unverified. Add tests for successful backup-code login and rejection of a second use.
